title: Trust in the Lord with all your heart
author: Proverbs
lines: Trust in the Lord with all your heart,
and don't lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him,
and he will make your paths straight.
why: The heart of Proverbs in two lines: wisdom begins by trusting someone wiser than yourself. Said in the morning, it turns the day's choices into a walk with God.

title: Love is strong as death
src: Song of Songs 8:6–7 · World English Bible
author: Song of Songs
lines: Set me as a seal on your heart,
as a seal on your arm;
for love is strong as death.
Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol.
Its flashes are flashes of fire,
a very flame of the Lord.
If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love,
why: The climax of the Bible's love poem, read at weddings and funerals alike: a love that floods cannot drown and money cannot buy.

title: In him all things are held together
author: Colossians
lines: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.

For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him.
He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.
why: Perhaps one of the oldest Christian hymns: what Proverbs said of Wisdom, this letter says of Christ. The last line is a whole way of seeing the world.
